title: Magna Carta Adventure
welcome_lead: In 1215 angry barons forced King John to seal the Magna Carta — a charter that limited the king's power. Let's see why it still matters. 📜
meta_desc: Magna Carta Adventure — a KS3 History walkthrough of 1215. King John, the barons and why the charter changed England.
final_note: You learned why the barons rebelled, what Magna Carta promised, and why 1215 is one of the most famous dates in English history.

walkthroughs.body_html:
King John ruled England from 1199 to 1216 — and he was not popular.

He lost wars in France, raised high taxes to pay for them, and ignored his barons' advice. He also argued with the Pope and was kicked out of the Church for a while.

By 1215 the barons had had enough. They raised an army and forced John to talk. ⚔️

On 15 June 1215, at a meadow called Runnymede by the River Thames, King John put his seal on the Magna Carta (Latin for 'Great Charter').

It had 63 clauses. The most important ones promised:

  • No new taxes without the barons' agreement
  • Free men could not be jailed without a fair trial
  • The king must obey the law too

Magna Carta did not give freedom to everyone — peasants got nothing from it. John even ignored it once the barons went home!

But it set out a huge idea: the rule of law. Even a king must follow the law.

That idea inspired later parliaments, the US Constitution and human rights law around the world. 🌍

mcqs.q: Why did Prohibition fail in the United States?
options: Widespread evasion via speakeasies and bootlegging, growth of organised crime, loss of tax revenue, and changing public opinion led to repeal in 1933.
Prohibition failed because the President personally banned the police from enforcing it.
Prohibition failed because most Americans were already alcoholics.
Because Britain had no army at all in the 1930s.

options: Because Chamberlain was a coward and admired Hitler.
Britain was militarily unprepared, traumatised by WWI losses, sympathetic to revising Versailles, and feared communism more than Nazism.
